why: Golden vectors for the family's owner claim, <host>@<os>:<pid>[:<startUnixSeconds>], written beside every test run's temp folder
(<folder>.owner). TWO writers exist today — OwnerClaim.Format/ForThisProcess in src_mcp/tests (C#) and claimText in
src_vs_code/scripts/run-tests.mjs (Node) — and ONE reader will exist (the conventions' Node sweeper, leftovers-E5). This file is read by
a C# test AND a Node test, so a change to one side's format turns that side red alone. E5's reader must pass the same vectors.
format: what the writers must produce for given parts (a host name cannot hold '@', ':' or whitespace: each becomes '-'; the start field
is present only when given). valid / invalid: what a STRICT reader accepts (no trimming: a trailing newline is not part of the claim).
linuxStart: how the Linux start field is computed from /proc/self/stat field 22 (ticks of 1/100 s since boot, counted after the LAST ')')
and the 'btime' line of /proc/stat — both writers use this formula; null means 'no start is better than a wrong one'.
